name: Texas Eastern NJ-NY Project
monitor_reason: length: gross 19.8 mi (Federal Register, FERC draft EIS notice) to 20.9 mi (EIA) is new AND replacement pipe; 8.95 mi of existing pipe is abandoned, so net new pipe is about 10.9 mi (17.5 km). The wholly new 30-inch Manhattan lateral is about 15.2 mi (24.5 km). Both are under the 25 km rule.
researcher_notes: No existing row matches. P0150 is the Algonquin AIM project and P0260 is TEAM 2014, both different. The project is real: Texas Eastern Transmission and Algonquin Gas Transmission, FERC docket CP11-56, up to 800,000 dekatherms per day, in service November 2013 per the EIA August 2026 release (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 761, 20.9 miles, 30 and 42 inch, cost 1,200 million USD). A FERC draft environmental impact statement notice from September 2011 in the Federal Register states about 19.8 miles of new and replacement 42 and 30 inch pipe and abandonment of 8.95 miles of existing pipe. A search summary says the 15.2 mile 30 inch line runs from Staten Island through Bayonne and Hoboken to lower Manhattan; that figure was not read on a verified page. Kept as monitor on length. If Baird rules that gross length counts, stage as an expansion row under Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO) Gas Pipeline with status operating, length 20.9 mi, capacity 800 MMcf/d (EIA), owners Texas Eastern and Algonquin; owner names not yet looked up. Confidence medium.
